discovery: Discovery of the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune

nominees.name: David C. Jewitt
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

subfield: Planetary physics and astrophysics of the Solar System
motivation: In 1992, after a five-year search that many thought hopeless, David Jewitt and Jane Luu detected 1992 QB1, the first object found in the trans-Neptunian region beyond Pluto. They used pioneering CCD surveys and careful motion-based detection to make faint, distant bodies measurable. Their discovery showed that the outer Solar System holds a vast disk of primordial icy bodies, the Kuiper Belt. This changed our physical picture of how planetary systems form and evolve. It explained where short-period comets come from and set Pluto in context. It also laid the empirical basis for planetary migration models and for the physics of debris disks around other stars. Their work opened a whole new region to physical study and directly led to missions such as New Horizons' flyby of Arrokoth. It is an example of persistent, data-driven discovery that transformed a field.
